To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
optogenetic stimulation of a single olfactory neuron type results in sparsened neuronal activity and more compact spatial representation of olfactory input in an olfactory glomerular unit.

(1) optogenetic activation of a single olfactory glomerular unit results in a small, spatially compact, and highly temporally precise response, (2) the spatial extent of this response does not increase with stimulus strength, and (3) the spatial extent and temporal precision of the response are maintained throughout the olfactory glomeruli, interneuron and mitral cell layers.

1) The glomerular unit is composed of a small population of neurons that respond to odor stimuli, 2) The glomerulus is a compact unit of olfactory processing that does not expand with increasing stimulus intensity, 3) The glomeruli of the main olfactory bulb are highly interconnected and form a functional network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how information is processed in the brain, in particular, in the olfactory bulb.
the question of how olfactory information is encoded in the olfactory bulb.
the processing of olfactory information in the glomerular network of the olfactory bulb.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optogenetic stimulation of a single olfactory glomerular input unit results in an optogenetic glomular response that is smaller in size, less widespread and less diverse in its neuronal composition compared to a natural odor stimulus.
the optogenetic glomeral unit response was significantly smaller than the response to the same intensity odour stimulus.
the optogenetically activated glomerular unit has a small and spatial compact response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the olfactory bulb is a highly dynamic and flexible structure that can adapt to different input stimuli and processing demands.
the glomerular layer is a site where sensory input is transformed to output.
the glomerular neuropil faithfully represents the input, but the output is sparsened.
The main takeaway from our work is that

optogenetic stimulation of a single olfactory neuron type can be used to study the unit function of a single olfferent glomerulus, but that this stimulation paradigm is likely to underestimate the full range of responses evoked by odor stimuli.
optogenetic stimulation can provide a more precise description of glomerulus function than odor stimulation.

the olfactory glomerular unit is not a simple relay of sensory input, but is a highly dynamic and complex circuit that transforms incoming sensory signals into a spatially compact and temporally precise representation.
